title: Zhejiang University reports first real-device QRAM on superconducting chip
summary: Zhejiang University researchers report that they demonstrated quantum random-access memory \(QRAM\) on a self-fabricated superconducting chip called Tianmu-2, describing it as the first real-device implementation and saying the work was published in Nature Physics. The chip ran 4-bit and 8-bit prototypes with 80.9% and 60.4% accuracy, respectively; the team also reports that optimized circuits reduced circuit depth by more than 30% and that the architecture showed local noise resilience. The team&\#x27;s next step is scaling QRAM, but the 8-bit accuracy remains modest and the first-demonstration claim comes from a single source.
